decision: target is the installed Wireshark 4.6.9 app bundle
why: the request names Wireshark and this machine has exactly one install
evidence: /Applications/Wireshark.app, `Wireshark --version` -> 4.6.9

decision: REA route is native-macos provider, not Hopper
why: Hopper is refused by macOS Automation permission
evidence: rea doctor --json: hopper healthy but `rea analyze` -> provider_unavailable, "macOS denied permission to send Apple events to Hopper"

decision: reuse tshark/dumpcap instead of reimplementing dissection
why: libwireshark.19.dylib is 245,574,112 bytes; tshark reports 3169 protocols and 272543 fields
evidence: rea inspect-macho ev_4b85c9b21a8fa5a1272918ef76619b51bc13e73c0edf4f43f809ca1d15442241; `tshark -G protocols | wc -l` -> 3169

decision: no sudo for capture
why: user is in access_bpf and /dev/bpf0 is group-writable
evidence: dumpcap -i en0 -c 5 -> "Packets captured: 5", exit 0

decision: stream format is `tshark -l -T ek -e ...`
why: newline-delimited JSON per packet, no separator ambiguity, streams live
evidence: first packet line at t+0.61s of a live en0 capture

decision: detail pane reads `tshark -r <cap> -Y "frame.number==N" -T json`; bytes read `-x`
why: both proven on the fixture, no dependence on unsettled sharkd methods
evidence: tshark -r Fixtures/sample-live.pcapng -T json -> layers frame,eth,ip,tcp; -x -> hex+ascii rows

decision: sharkd is out of scope for now
why: `frames`/`frame` params are member-name lists and the probing run desynced; not settled
evidence: sharkd: `frames` -> "frame is not a valid member name"; `frame`+tree -> "tree is not a valid member name"

decision: UI is a native SwiftUI app built by SPM
why: Xcode 27.1 and Swift 6.4 are present; Wireshark is a native desktop app
evidence: probe package built in 11.26s and wrote its window callback; process stayed alive

decision: Swift language mode v5 for the package
why: 4 parallel delegates on strict v6 concurrency would spend their budget on Sendable errors, not on the scanner
evidence: probe built clean under v6; v5 chosen for throughput only

decision: seven units, one writer each
why: units are separable by directory and each ends in one command
evidence: .poteto/queue.md

decision: verification uses recorded tshark output, not crafted pcaps
why: deterministic and offline; the live path is proven separately by smoke-live
evidence: Fixtures/sample-live.{pcapng,fields.tsv,tree.json,hex.txt}

decision: gate `swift test --filter X` compiles every test target, so one owner's mid-edit file blocks all owners
why: SwiftPM builds one test bundle per package; module isolation did not isolate test targets
evidence: suspicion-dev and attrib-dev both blocked by Tests/SentinelIdentityTests and Tests/SentinelSuspicionTests mid-edit states
result: rule added: keep `swift build --build-tests` at exit 0 between edits; a sibling blocker means poll up to 5 times, not stop

decision: briefed certificate field names do not exist
why: `tshark -G fields` lists no tls.handshake.certificate_subject or _issuer
evidence: tshark -G fields | grep -qx tls.handshake.certificate_subject -> MISSING
result: task-2 corrected to revision 3 before implementation landed

decision: certificate evidence is opportunistic, never required
why: TLS 1.3 encrypts the Certificate message, so x509sat.* is empty on modern connections
evidence: curl https://example.com -> handshake types 1,2 only; with --tls-max 1.2 -> types 1,2,11,12,14,16 and uTF8String carries example.com
result: identity must fall back to SNI/DNS/Host and must not invent a name

decision: x509af.subject and x509af.issuer are unusable as names
why: they return numeric OID lists, not strings
evidence: tshark -r /tmp/tls12-raw.pcapng -T fields -e x509af.subject -> "0,0,0,0"
result: readable names come from x509sat.uTF8String / printableString

decision: suspicion-dev committed 461b52a outside the lead
why: teammates share git identity DSH Lead <lead@dsh.local>, so a teammate commit is indistinguishable from a lead commit
evidence: git log --format shows one author for all commits; suspension-dev confirmed ownership of 461b52a
result: rule added: no git write commands from owners; the lead commits one unit per commit

decision: task-3 accepted: 8 tests, 0 failures
why: the behavioural claim is settled by a real loopback socket attributed to the test's own pid
evidence: attrib-dev gate output at 2ecb830, plus a negative control that dropped the remote-port match and watched the test fail

decision: task-4 accepted: 17 tests, 0 failures
why: beaconing, inbound unsolicited and unsigned-process rules are asserted in both directions
evidence: suspicion-dev gate output at 2ecb830

decision: app populates FlowObservation.hasLocalListener from the real listener table
why: task-4's inboundUnsolicited rule is over-eager without a producer, so every inbound flow would be flagged
evidence: `suspicion-dev` reported no producer; app parser output equals lsof ground truth exactly (28 ports, identical sets)
result: hostname: `WiresharkSentinel --check-listeners` equals the awk-extracted lsof port set

decision: assessment work moved off the main actor
why: attributor.refresh() runs lsof and codesign and measured 0.272s in the task-3 suite; every 2s on the main thread would stall the window
evidence: attrib-dev's own test measured 0.272s for one attribution pass
result: reassess snapshots flows, then runs lsof and assessment in a detached task

decision: publish packets in batches instead of one @Published append per packet
why: per-packet publishing made SwiftUI re-diff the table, throttling ingest
evidence: controlled back-to-back: raw tshark 2153 packets vs app 919 in the same 15s; after batching 2237 vs 2135
result: committed 60f0873 and 0d846ad; conversations found rose from 24 to 35

decision: direction comes from the TCP handshake and the port roles, not packet order
why: capture starts mid-conversation, so a server reply was read as an inbound connection and accused the user's own browser
evidence: report said "Inbound connection to this Mac" for 3.173.21.63:443 while the raw capture shows an outbound SYN to 443
result: engine task-6 added tcp.flags; app uses TCPFlags.synOnly plus service-port roles

decision: aggregate conversations by remote service, not by the whole 5-tuple
why: every DNS query from a fresh ephemeral port became its own conversation
evidence: 192.168.1.254:53 appeared 16 times as separate conversations; now once

decision: engine values are "True"/"False", not "1"/"true"
why: my brief asserted the wrong value shape; engine-dev measured the real one
